chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah ibn Mihrān, who said:

I asked him about a virgin slave-girl at the beginning of when she menstruates: she remains in the month for two days, and in another month for three days; it varies for her, and her menses are not the same number of days each month. He said: "She may sit and leave the salat (prayer) as long as she sees blood, so long as it does not exceed ten days. Then, when two months agree on the same number of days, those are her days."

key_terms.الدَّمَ: blood seen during the menstrual period
key_terms.الْبِكْرِ: virgin; one who has not previously been married or sexually active
key_terms.الْجَارِيَةِ: a young female, here referring to a young girl/slave-girl
key_terms.الْعَشَرَةَ: ten days, the upper limit mentioned in this ruling

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a girl whose menstrual days are irregular at the beginning of puberty?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a young woman at the onset of menstruation whose bleeding pattern is still irregular. She leaves salat (prayer) for as long as she sees menstrual blood up to ten days, and once the same number of days repeats for two months, that recurring number becomes her established cycle.
